0 Catopomp In Catopomp, you are the new supervisor of a team of cat psychopomps. To ensure that no lost souls are left behind, you must lead your furry subordinates to guide these souls into the afterlife. The goal of the game is to play all your cards and not be the last player with unplayed cards. Whenever you play cards from your hand, you must also reveal one additional card and place it in front of yourself. Over time, this will form a set of revealed cards that you will need to play as well. To help you with your task, once per round, you can use one or two dice from a shared pool to enhance your playing set. Time the dice well, and use them wisely! If you choose to pass, the player who played the most recent strongest set of cards can pass one of their revealed cards to you. This means that you will have more cards to clear. Yikes! What will you reveal? How will you manage your hidden and revealed cards? Finding the balance is key! [Rating: 1/10] Not a fan. Being 4th player, I had to pass the first 3 turns with no legal plays. Just not fun and doesn’t feel strategic.

[Rating: 5/10] Love the art, and it's a pretty good climber; my rating could go up if I play more. But will I play more? I've seen at least one other climber in this genre recently (where you can see part of the opponent's hand, and therefore have some idea what they can play) and I think it turns out that I really like just not knowing.  On the other hand, the dice mechanics are flexible enough to give only partial information about opponent plans, and I think I like that aspect better.  [1 play]

[Rating: 6/10] Played on BGA.  It’s a trick taker with some extra mechanics thrown in and nicely drawn cat art.  Mechanics I think the idea of having to plan around building a discard pile + the centrally drafted die are both unique ideas but the question is do they add to the fun or are they clunky. For me it felt more on the clunky side. This feels like one of those games you have to play half a dozen times to ‘get it’ but i didn’t really want to. Almost after the first trick you can already tell if you’ve won or lost but you still have to sit through the whole rest of the round. Also at 3 rounds this game

Game is incomplete so this review might change in the future when I have the chance to play a full game.  First impression would be how stunning the artwork is. Cats and soul are interesting combination that yields amazing result.  I tend to be very critical when it comes to the mechanics of a small box games because there are a lot of top tier small box games out there. [Rating: 9/10] A decent card shedding game with some new twists. Would play it again as a filler for my next gaming session.

[Rating: 9/10] Played the demo during ABGF 2025, and I thoroughly enjoyed it with my friends! The mechanics are interesting, and the rules are easy to digest. Can't wait to play it again in my next session!

[Rating: 9/10] Very interesting mechanics. The "Heaven and Hell" card management and dice provide a lot more flexibility than other games in this genre.

[Rating: 10/10] Played this during one of its public playtesting/demo sessions. It's easy to learn and has more tactical decision-making than expected! I would highly recommend this for players who want a light and crunchy game.

[Rating: 10/10] What a lovely little card game! It may be a slow burner for people who are not used to this genre of card games and mechanism at first. However, once you got the hang of it, it is smooth like butter! There's definitely more than meets the eye.   Can't wait for the game to be released soon : )
